outcome: Burungale, Skinner, Tian and Wan (arXiv:2409.01350, 'Zeta elements for elliptic curves and applications', Sept 2024) proved the p-part of the BSD conjecture at supersingular primes for elliptic curves of analytic rank 0 or 1, which combined with prior results yields the first infinite families of quadratic twists of non-CM elliptic curves over Q for which the full strong BSD conjecture holds unconditionally. This is a partial result (infinite but density-zero families, not the general conjecture), by four leading experts in Iwasawa theory, but as of this research it remains a preprint with no journal publication, expert blog digestion, or Quanta-style writeup found — so it is classified as a strong, credible claim rather than a community-vetted resolution. A follow-up computational paper (Banwait-Huang, arXiv:2601.16044, Jan 2026, to appear at ANTS XVII) applied an explicit algorithm to the LMFDB to identify 36,687 elliptic curves of conductor ≤ 500,000 (about 0.1% of the database) admitting such infinite families, but this is an application/identification exercise, not new theory, and does not itself change the status. No AI system was involved in either paper.
summary: The main-line development on BSD since the frozen revision date is Burungale-Skinner-Tian-Wan's September 2024 preprint (arXiv:2409.01350), which constructs p-adic zeta elements for elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields and uses them to prove the ±-main conjecture of Iwasawa theory at supersingular primes (Kobayashi's 2002 conjecture) for semistable elliptic curves, together with the p-part of the BSD formula at supersingular primes for analytic rank 0 or 1. Combined with earlier ordinary-prime results (Skinner-Urban, Wei Zhang, Burungale-Tian p-converse theorems), this yields the first known infinite families of quadratic twists of non-CM elliptic curves over Q for which the full strong BSD conjecture (rank equality plus the exact leading-coefficient formula, including finiteness of Sha) is unconditionally true. This is squarely a case of the stated problem: it settles BSD for an explicit infinite (but density-zero, roughly 0.1% by the follow-up paper's count) family of curves, leaving the general conjecture open — a textbook 'case settled' rather than resolution, so under a stricter reading it would be `partial`; I classify it `claimed` instead because it also has not yet cleared expert digestion (no journal acceptance, no Tao blog post, no Quanta piece found via search) despite being four years past submission and by highly credible authors (Skinner and Tian are established BSD/Iwasawa-theory specialists), and per the DEEP_DIVE rules 'resolved versus claimed turns on whether a human expert has read the argument' — I could not confirm that has happened publicly. I checked for follow-on validation: a January 2026 paper by Banwait and Huang (arXiv:2601.16044, accepted to ANTS XVII, a peer-reviewed algorithmic number theory venue) explicitly builds on and cites BSTW's theorem as an input to an algorithmic search of the LMFDB, treating the BSTW result as an established fact — this is suggestive of acceptance by specialists but is not itself a digestion of the BSTW proof. No AI system is mentioned in either paper; both are purely human theoretical/computational number theory. I also checked the several 2025 preprints claiming full proofs of BSD found by the triage (Zenodo/Shimizu, SSRN/Svancara 'Relational Field Theory', preprints.org 'Iran Formula') — these show classic crank hallmarks (self-published, unreviewed, grandiose framing, solo authors, no institutional affiliation signals of note) and none disclose any AI involvement; the preprints.org page returned HTTP 403 and could not be directly verified, so I could not rule out AI involvement there, but there is no positive evidence for it either, and per DEEP_DIVE.md's rule on unreachable pages I note this as a dead end rather than a verified finding.
competing_reading: A stricter reading of §3.1/§6.1 would call the BSTW result `partial` rather than `claimed`: it is unambiguously a case of the problem (an infinite family of curves), and 'claimed' is defined primarily for results awaiting digestion of a claimed *resolution* of the stated problem, whereas here nobody is claiming the general BSD conjecture is proved — only a genuine partial result is on the table, and partial results by leading experts in a serious preprint are ordinarily accepted as fact by the field well before formal journal publication (as evidenced by Banwait-Huang treating it as citable, peer-reviewed-venue-accepted, established input). Under that reading the status should be `partial` with `resolution_direction: confirmed`, dated to the same September 2024 event.
what_would_settle_it: Journal acceptance of arXiv:2409.01350, or an expert digestion (a Tao-style blog post, a Bourbaki seminar writeup, an ICM survey lecture, or a Quanta/AMS Notices piece) explicitly discussing the proof, would move this from `claimed` to a confirmed classification (whether `partial` or `resolved` in nature) rather than leaving the human-verification question open.

corrections.why: SCOPE: `claimed` counted the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture among resolutions and the site labelled it 'Proved (claimed)'. The record's own outcome calls Burungale-Skinner-Tian-Wan 'a partial result (infinite but density-zero families, not the general conjecture)', and its competing_reading argues for `partial`. Nobody claims the general conjecture; a case settled is `partial` under 6.1. The research rules fold 'how much was settled' and 'has an expert checked it' into one field, and the agent read an unreviewed case as `claimed`; that is the pattern this batch of corrections fixes. `partial` does not record review status, so the absence of expert digestion stays in `summary`.
